about: How this project tuned each function: what was tried, what happened, what was kept or rejected, and what has not been tried. Every entry cites the document it comes from; numbers are quoted as the sources state them. Dates are the journal's own where it gives one; where the text gives none (entries 1-21, the development sweeps), the date is the day the commit that recorded the work was made.

functions.extraction: Extraction: models reading symbols and tags
functions.line_tracing: Line tracing and connectivity (tracer, parent rule, flow direction, sheet stitching)
functions.scoring: Scoring: the scorer and its controls
functions.generated_pids: Generated P&IDs drawn from a model (loops, stations, style)
functions.te_model: Tennessee Eastman model: source and topology verification, tag conventions
functions.replay_and_bands: Replay, normal bands and fault detection
functions.ignition: Ignition and PI outputs: build, verifier, acceptance, screens
functions.real_unit: The real unit (Bayer residue treater): model from text, Figure 10/11 checks, replay
functions.review_loop: Review loop: operations corrections, mapping, outside review
functions.intake_and_reuse: Intake and reuse: runbook, DEXPI route, loop audit, CSV tools, vendor kit

attempts.change: Round-1 first try: Claude, GPT (Codex) and Gemini read the 12 OPEN100 drawings whole-sheet with the first prompt (bare [x, y, x, y] box lists).
attempts.evidence: Found + right class F1: Codex 0.87, Claude 0.85, Gemini 0.44; connections F1 0.56 / 0.43 / 0.15 (out/scorecard_first-try.md).
attempts.why: The first-try numbers stay the published headline, but prompt v2 replaced this prompt for every later run.

attempts.change: Ran the identical first prompt a second time on the same 12 drawings to measure run-to-run noise.
attempts.evidence: Codex 0.87 -> 0.87, Claude 0.85 -> 0.85, Gemini 0.44 -> 0.57; Claude and Codex move about ±0.03 between runs, first-try Gemini ±0.13.
attempts.why: Measuring noise before claiming a difference became a standing rule, and the Gemini swing exposed its format problem.

attempts.change: Prompt v2: named box fields (x_min, y_min, ...) instead of a bare [x, y, x, y] list.
attempts.hypothesis: Gemini's gap was mostly an output-format problem (axis order), not vision.
attempts.evidence: Gemini 0.44 -> 0.74 found + right class; Codex 0.87 -> 0.85, Claude 0.85 -> 0.85. On 5 of 12 drawings Gemini's boxes scored about 0 as delivered and 0.60-0.92 with the axes swapped back.
attempts.why: Format-only fix applied to every tool; it became the prompt for all later rounds. Written after seeing all 12 drawings, which bends the held-out rule (stated in EVALUATION.md rule 7).

attempts.change: Gemma 4 31B (open weights, hosted API) as the offline stand-in: prompt v2, same 12 drawings, 30-minute client timeout.
attempts.evidence: 5 of 12 calls hit the 30-minute timeout and scored 0: found + right class F1 0.25, connections 0.02. On the 7 that completed, found F1 about 0.54 with precision 0.93.
attempts.why: Kept as the honest first-try headline; the docs leave the offline choice to a site's own tuning and measurement.

attempts.change: Gemma retry with a 90-minute timeout on the 5 timed-out drawings (labelled as a retry).
attempts.evidence: Drawings 5 and 6 completed in about 4 minutes (F1 0.38 and 0.55); drawings 0, 9 and 10 timed out again, the same three both times. Across both attempts 9 of 12 completed, about 0.53 found F1 against about 0.90 for the frontier models.
attempts.why: Consistent with the model or the hosted service stalling on certain images; which one cannot be told from outside.

attempts.change: Applied the selected whole-sheet recipe (gpt-6.1-sol, original prompt) to two development sheets of a separate labelled collection, PID2Graph Synthetic, through native workers.
attempts.evidence: Review load 47 / 108 = 43.52 per 100; located 42 / 43 symbols; source-class F1 0.424 micro; connections 44 TP / 45 predicted / 65 key. 24 corrections are source-class disagreements, 20 of them source `general`.
attempts.why: Two development sheets identify gaps (label vocabulary, line semantics), not broad performance.

attempts.change: Prospective frozen trial: the unchanged whole-sheet recipe on the two never-opened Synthetic sheets 2 and 3, scored once after sealing.
attempts.evidence: 73 corrections / 158 key items = 46.20 per 100; 47 / 49 symbols located; rough source-class F1 0.625; connection P/R/F1 0.951 / 0.532 / 0.682.
attempts.why: A transfer measurement with no tuning or repair; both sheets are now consumed, so a changed method needs new data.

attempts.change: Equipment schedules printed along the bottom of each OPEN100 sheet transcribed by Claude to supply equipment purposes.
attempts.evidence: 49 of the 74 purpose cards come from the schedules.
attempts.why: The extraction never read the schedules; they say what each piece of equipment is for. Not checked by a second model.

attempts.change: Round 5 replicates: five fresh runs of the declared method M3 per model on holdout A.
attempts.hypothesis: How much does M3 move between runs, and is the GPT-Claude gap bigger than that?
attempts.evidence: GPT 20.1 (runs 18.3-21.8 / bootstrap 14.2-28.0), Claude 29.8 (27.5-32.1 / 12.8-47.3); run SD 1.4 and 1.9 points against the ~1 point round 2 assumed. GPT minus Claude -9.8: runs interval -12.2 to -7.3, bootstrap -26.5 to +4.5, a tie by the pre-registered rule.
attempts.why: The five-run means replaced the round-2 single runs as the quoted holdout-A figures; the round-2 verdict stands because its ~30-point gain is far outside the noise.

attempts.change: Round 5: declared method M3 on five DEXPI example sheets from a different publisher (a third drafting style).
attempts.hypothesis: Does M3 carry over to drawings from a different publisher?
attempts.evidence: Review load GPT 95.4, Claude 61.8 against about 20-30 on holdout A, outside both tools' holdout-A bootstrap intervals. GPT bimodal on C01: nozzles reported in 3 of 5 runs (143.5-146.8) and not in 2 (32-34).
attempts.why: The method does worse on this source, much of it key scope (nozzles); nothing was changed because a fix would be a new method needing unseen drawings.

attempts.change: Tracer first cut: split 4-arm crossings, band 0.15, no through-line handling or barrier.
attempts.evidence: Oracle (answer-key boxes) review load 15.2 on dev.
attempts.why: Starting point for the variant sweep.

attempts.change: Join crossings (the key treats crossings as pass-through), band 0.15.
attempts.evidence: Dev review load oracle 12.2 / Claude 34.3 / Codex 43.9 / Gemini 131.4.
attempts.why: Joining crossings matches the key's definition; kept in the final defaults.

attempts.change: Band 0.05 x median symbol side (crossings joined).
attempts.evidence: Oracle 9.8 / Claude 32.5 / Codex 36.6 / Gemini 120.3.
attempts.why: Kept in the final defaults.

attempts.change: Wider band 0.3 / 0.5.
attempts.evidence: Claude 39.5 / 51.6, Codex 45.8 / 60.1, Gemini 138.3 / 152.5 (oracle column 17.2 / 21.3 at 0.25 / 0.4 with crossings split).
attempts.why: Worse for every tool.

attempts.change: line_frac 0.3 / 0.6 / 1.0 with crossings joined.
attempts.evidence: Oracle 9.8 in all three.
attempts.why: No effect.

attempts.change: Drop boxes that a straight line runs through (through-line boxes).
attempts.evidence: Oracle 14.7 / Claude 36.5 / Codex 39.6 / Gemini 117.5.
attempts.why: Worse than keeping them.

attempts.change: Snap through-line boxes to the remaining ink.
attempts.evidence: Oracle 9.8 / Claude 32.2 / Codex 36.1 / Gemini 117.1.
attempts.why: Small gain; kept as through-line snap.

attempts.change: Missed-symbol barrier, size only, 0.3 x symbol side.
attempts.evidence: Oracle 9.5 / Claude 34.3 / Codex 37.8 / Gemini 80.0.
attempts.why: It blocks nozzles.

attempts.change: Missed-symbol barrier, size only, 0.5 / 0.8 x side.
attempts.why: Not adopted; the final barrier adds a stroke test at 0.3 side (the table gives no separate verdict).

attempts.change: Missed-symbol barrier at 0.3 x side, only for blobs with < 60% orthogonal strokes (the final default).
attempts.evidence: Oracle 9.6 / Claude 29.8 / Codex 34.4 / Gemini 87.6.
attempts.why: Final tracer default.

attempts.change: Barrier variants: < 40% orthogonal; 0.2 side; compact blobs only; size cap 2 / 3 / 5 sides.
attempts.why: None beat the final barrier across tools; compact-only is marked rejected in the sweep table.

attempts.change: Final settings but split 4-arm crossings.
attempts.evidence: Oracle 17.9 / Claude 45.8 / Codex 40.3 / Gemini 83.9.
attempts.why: Worse for the oracle, Claude and Codex.

attempts.change: Nearest-neighbour tree per network instead of linking all pairs.
attempts.evidence: Oracle 45.5 / Claude 60.5 / Codex 62.3 / Gemini 81.5.
attempts.why: Best for Gemini only.

attempts.change: All pairs only up to 6 / 12 symbols per network, else a tree.
attempts.why: Worse than all pairs for the oracle, Claude and Codex.

attempts.change: Final settings with band 0.1 / 0.2.
attempts.why: Slightly worse than band 0.05.

attempts.change: Union: tracer links plus the model's own links.
attempts.evidence: Claude 35.4-37.7, Codex 41.6-45.5, Gemini 97-103 against tracer-only 29.8 / 34.4 / 87.6.
attempts.why: Adding the model's links added false links faster than true ones.

attempts.change: M2: tracer connections on the whole-sheet (M0) symbols.
attempts.hypothesis: Connections were every model's weakest point; lines are geometry, which code does deterministically.
attempts.evidence: Review load dev / holdout A / holdout B: Codex 34.4 / 28.7 / 16.2, Claude 29.8 / 36.0 / 28.2, Gemini 87.6 / 55.4 / 83.9.
attempts.why: Lost to M3 on holdout A for every tool; for Codex it beat M3 on holdout B (16.2 vs 20.7), reported, not acted on.

attempts.change: M3: tracer connections on the tiled (M1) symbols; the declared method.
attempts.hypothesis: Give geometry to deterministic code and keep the model for symbols and tags.
attempts.evidence: Holdout A: Codex 48.8 -> 17.8, Claude 61.1 -> 32.4, Gemini 75.9 -> 40.2; holdout B: 67.0 -> 20.7, 76.6 -> 16.5, 92.7 -> 38.3. Codex connection recall 55% -> 88% at 89% precision.
attempts.why: Lowest holdout-A review load for every tool and better than M0 on holdout B, so not style overfitting by the pre-registered rule. Later five-run means: GPT 20.1, Claude 29.8.

attempts.change: Round-2 twin: instrument parent = asset sharing its traced pipe network (`linked`).
attempts.evidence: Holdout A parent accuracy 87.0% (134/154) against round 1's 90.9% (140/154) and a position-only control of 85.7%; holdout B 70.8% (286/404).
attempts.why: A better connection score made the twin's parent choice worse; replaced by the along-line rule, kept as the second opinion.

attempts.change: Round-3 parent rule: nearest non-instrument asset reached by following the drawn line (`along_line`).
attempts.hypothesis: Choosing the parent by distance along the traced line fixes the round-2 regression.
attempts.evidence: Dev 92.6%; holdout A 92.2% (142/154), beating both 87.0% and 90.9% (margin over round 1 is 2 instruments); holdout B 67.6% (273/404), worse than `linked`'s 70.8%.
attempts.why: Meets the pre-registered win on holdout A; fixed for this drafting style, not in general, so disagreements with `linked` go to review.

attempts.change: Legacy tracer replacing raw whole-sheet links on the exposed Synthetic sheets 2/3.
attempts.evidence: True collapsed links 58 -> 48, false links 3 -> 5.
attempts.why: The tracer follows connected ink; dotted and dashed strokes are separate components.

attempts.change: Broad-close diagnostic: 15% symbol-side axis closing before the unchanged tracer.
attempts.evidence: TP / false per Synthetic sheet 0-3: 38/6, 25/5, 73/0, 29/10. Disabling through-line snap did not change these counts.
attempts.why: No repeated-dash evidence and more false joins.

attempts.change: Selective interior-only dash recovery at 15% gap / 30% dash, no guard, scored as a union with raw links.
attempts.evidence: 29/0, 25/1, 50/0, 28/7 (union diagnostic).
attempts.why: Union values were not adopted as the traced headline.

attempts.change: Added symbol guard, fixed 25% gap / 50% dash, traced-only; then guarded attachment boxes.
attempts.why: Intermediate steps toward the final development v2 geometry.

attempts.change: Development v2 tracer: repeated-dash recovery with qualified endpoint extension and guarded symbol barriers (opt-in stage).
attempts.evidence: 27/0, 19/0, 48/0, 23/7. Exposed sheets 2/3: 71 TP / 7 FP / 38 FN against raw 58/3/51; missed-plus-false corrections 54 -> 45, but sheets 1 and 3 regress against raw extraction.
attempts.why: Sequential tuning on exposed development data; not a universal replacement or a prospective result.

attempts.change: Flow direction v1: an arrowhead orients every symbol behind it against every symbol ahead of it.
attempts.evidence: 380 conflicts, still 237 after instrument links were taken out.
attempts.why: On a header with two outlets it says A flows to B and back; the conflicts showed the rule was wrong.

attempts.change: Flow direction final: first-hand evidence (arrow or flag on the pipe between two symbols, no branch between) kept apart from across-a-branch evidence; pump ports; valve continuity.
attempts.evidence: 361 of 1,133 process links directed (32%), 101 conflicts shown without arrow. Arrowhead detection on held-out sheets 6-11: 83% precision, 77% recall of key arrow nodes. Blind spot check of 65 crops: neither GPT nor Claude disagreed with the code; arrowheads and flags agree on 70 of 70 shared links.
attempts.why: Each link carries the lower end of the 95% interval for its source as confidence; two-thirds of process links stay undirected.

attempts.change: Read drawing numbers written with en dashes ("PID 110–1") as numbers for off-page connector pairing.
attempts.evidence: 31 more connectors found their sheet: 38 sheet-to-sheet connections instead of 7.
attempts.why: En dashes had defeated the twin's connector pairing.

attempts.change: Diagnostic on DEXPI: the models' own links without tracing (M1) against M3.
attempts.evidence: M1 review load GPT 79.3, Claude 65.0; with tracing 95.4 and 61.8.
attempts.why: Tracing helped Claude a little and hurt GPT, mostly through the nozzle runs; labelled diagnostic.

attempts.change: Diagnostic: pad equipment boxes by 4 px (the outline width) before tracing revision C.
attempts.hypothesis: Claude's higher L1/L2 load comes from tight vessel boxes letting the tracer follow the wall.
attempts.evidence: Removes every extra Claude link: sheet 101 connections 0.93 -> 0.99, sheet 103 0.86 -> 1.00; no change for GPT.
attempts.why: A method change; the published scores stay as measured until it is measured on every result it would touch.

attempts.change: 2x2 grid chosen by running the tile stitching on the answer key itself, not by sweeping grids against the score.
attempts.evidence: A perfect model still loses ~10% of links at 2x2 seams.
attempts.why: Choosing the grid from the key's own geometry avoids tuning the grid to the score.

attempts.change: M1: 2x2 overlapping tiles (15% overlap), seam-aware de-duplication, the model's own links only.
attempts.hypothesis: Small symbols and tags get lost when a 3,000-pixel sheet is downscaled.
attempts.evidence: Dev review load Claude 73.5 / Codex 46.3 / Gemini 76.1 (baseline 66.4 / 66.5 / 90.8); holdout A 54.9 / 31.7 / 68.0; holdout B 71.5 / 64.8 / 80.2. Tiling made Claude worse on dev and better on both holdouts.
attempts.why: Tiling is kept as the symbol source of M3; tiles-only connections lost to M3 on holdout A for every tool.

attempts.change: Optional whole-sheet links added onto the tiled symbols (the `-ov` runs: the same model's whole-sheet answer contributes connections only).
attempts.evidence: Dev review load Claude 72.8 / Codex 44.6 / Gemini 80.4, repeat 72.5 / 44.9 / 79.2, against tiles-only 73.5 / 46.3 / 76.1 and repeat 72.8 / 46.9 / 75.1.
attempts.why: Not part of the declared M1 or M3; the docs record no reason, and the differences are a few points either way.

attempts.change: Diagnostic: M1 (tiles only) run five times per model on holdout A.
attempts.evidence: GPT 36.7 (round 2's single run: 31.7), Claude 53.0 (54.9).
attempts.why: Labelled diagnostic, not pre-registered; nothing was changed.

attempts.change: Use the model's own confidence to rank items for review.
attempts.evidence: Two of three models report 0.9-1.0 confidence for nearly everything; the fitted risk model gave self-confidence a weight of zero.
attempts.why: It ranks nothing; it remains only the baseline the risk rating must beat.

attempts.change: Risk rating from independent cross-checks (peer-model agreement, whole-sheet vs tiled self-agreement, on-a-line, tag form), one non-negative logistic regression each for symbols (10 signals) and links (7), fit on dev only.
attempts.hypothesis: Independent evidence ranks errors better than self-reported confidence.
attempts.evidence: Riskiest 20% held more errors than own-confidence ordering in 23 of 24 holdout comparisons, usually 2-4x; green precision 94-96% (A) and 97-100% (B); error rates rise green -> amber -> red everywhere. Fails for Codex M3 on holdout A: 40% vs 43%.
attempts.why: Calibrated and useful except for the declared tool and method, where agreement punishes the model that is right alone.

attempts.change: Candidate risk signals: placeholder tags, duplicate tags, the `general` class, network size.
attempts.evidence: Each received a fitted weight of zero on the development sheets.
attempts.why: They did not help rank errors (placeholders are real symbols with an unassigned tag).

attempts.change: Parent second opinion: build the twin with both parent rules and flag an instrument when `along_line` and `linked` pick different equipment.
attempts.evidence: On dev this happened to about 1 instrument in 20, and the along-line choice was right in 16 of 18 such cases.
attempts.why: Turns a rule that only half-generalized into a review question instead of a silent choice.

attempts.change: Round 4, L1 photocopy degradation of holdout A, declared M3 unchanged.
attempts.hypothesis: Where does the method break as image quality drops: the models' reading or the code tracer?
attempts.evidence: Review load GPT 17.8 -> 20.6, Claude 32.4 -> 29.7; connection F1 0.87 / 0.79.
attempts.why: No consistent change (small, opposite directions); measurement only, no decision rides on it.

attempts.change: Round 4, L2 old-scan degradation.
attempts.evidence: Review load GPT 51.5, Claude 57.0; symbols rough F1 0.87 / 0.86; connection F1 0.51 / 0.45.
attempts.why: About 3x the clean review load; measurement only.

attempts.change: Round 4, L3 bad-scan degradation.
attempts.evidence: Review load GPT 72.6, Claude 70.6; symbols 0.77 / 0.81; connections 0.22 / 0.19, below the models' own untraced links (0.36).
attempts.why: About 4x; the tracer is hurting at this level; measurement only.

attempts.change: Isolating comparison: L3 symbols, tracer run on the clean image.
attempts.evidence: Review load GPT 60.7, Claude 47.9; connection F1 recovers to 0.53 / 0.63.
attempts.why: Localised the failure in the code tracer, not the models; nothing was tuned.

attempts.change: First tag-text measurement: M3 on the three DEXPI XML sheets (33 labelled symbols) and the two list-keyed C08 sheets (145 identifiers).
attempts.evidence: Strict: GPT 29 of 33 (0.879), Claude 28 of 33 (0.848), identical in all five runs; both 20 of 20 on C01. C08 lists: GPT 100%, Claude 99.4%. Lenient matching gave the same as strict.
attempts.why: Clean vector drawings only; misses are vertical, multi-line and actuator-bubble labels. Says nothing about scans.

attempts.change: TE revision A round trip, clean sheets: M3 on the generated house-style sheets.
attempts.evidence: Both models read all 43 printed tags in every run; review load GPT 2.1, Claude 2.2 (2.1-2.6).
attempts.why: A round trip on our own drawings: an upper bound, not real-plant accuracy.

attempts.change: TE revision A round trip on degraded copies L1-L3.
attempts.evidence: Tags read exactly at L2: GPT 56%, Claude 95%; at L3: GPT 14%, Claude 49%. Review load L3 16.9 / 17.3.
attempts.why: Text fails before shapes; the models fail differently, no winner called.

attempts.change: Revision C read-back (controllers, signal lines, valve stations) with the entry-44 protocol.
attempts.evidence: Clean review load GPT 1.26, Claude 1.38, tags 100%. L2 tags 61% / 89%, L3 9% / 50%. GPT controller tags misread at L2: 51% against 34% for other tags.
attempts.why: Smaller text inside the DCS symbol costs readability on poor copies; scores kept as measured.

attempts.change: First scorer rule: a predicted box centre landing near the key box counts as a match.
attempts.evidence: With every class deliberately wrong it still gave 15-32% credit.
attempts.why: Mislabelled valves landed in a neighbouring instrument's zone; small symbols sat inside tanks' boxes.

attempts.change: Tightened centre-distance rule.
attempts.evidence: Wrong-class control still scored 3-20%.
attempts.why: The rule itself was wrong, not the setting.

attempts.change: IoU matching: strict IoU >= 0.5 and rough IoU >= 0.1, six asset classes only.
attempts.evidence: The every-class-wrong control scores about 0.
attempts.why: Frozen scorer for all later rounds.

attempts.change: The 'moved' negative control that also shrank every box to 1x1.
attempts.evidence: It passed for the wrong reason: a 1x1 box can never overlap under IoU.
attempts.why: Fixed to keep box sizes.

attempts.change: Half-sheet shift control on repetitive drawing 6.
attempts.evidence: Strict score 0, rough score 8.8% (two identical pump details half a sheet apart).
attempts.why: Kept as an honest chance floor for the rough score on repetitive sheets, documented rather than hidden.

attempts.change: Score only the six asset classes; leave drawing plumbing unscored.
attempts.evidence: The key has 10 classes; 2,408 line-bend points, 734 crossings, 451 arrows and 48 frames are excluded.
attempts.why: Plumbing matters to drawing, not to a twin.

attempts.change: Primary score 'review load': corrections per 100 key items, written before round 2.
attempts.evidence: Baseline M0 holdout A: Codex 48.8, Claude 61.1, Gemini 75.9.
attempts.why: Counts differences from the answer key, not timed reviewer corrections (entry 60 states this plainly).

attempts.change: Report a bootstrap interval over drawings beside the runs-only interval, with bootstrap as the headline for model comparisons.
attempts.evidence: Runs interval called GPT better on holdout A (-12.2 to -7.3); bootstrap -26.5 to +4.5 made it a tie.
attempts.why: Six drawings, not run noise, are the real limit.

attempts.change: Replicate summary as first written: an interval of zero width counted as 'different'.
attempts.evidence: Called the tag difference different, though every run had the same score.
attempts.why: Now reports 'no run-to-run variation' in that case, with a test.

attempts.change: DEXPI key adapter checked by scoring the key against itself before any model ran.
attempts.evidence: Found three problems: column sections counted as a second tank, zero-area flange/blind boxes, an area-prefix line joined to a tag; after the fixes the key scores zero corrections.
attempts.why: Fixes recorded in the pre-registration before the first model call.

attempts.change: README headline 'symbols F1 0.97, connections 0.89' from the single round-2 run.
attempts.evidence: The five-run means are 0.93 and 0.87; check_claims.py found it on its first run.
attempts.why: Replaced by the five-run means; claims are now checked against result files in CI.

attempts.change: Scorer command line given a run record instead of a bare prediction.
attempts.evidence: Scored the run record as zero; found by the timing run.
attempts.why: Now unwraps `prediction`, or refuses a file with no symbols.

attempts.change: Revision A: TE model drawn as three sheets in the house style measured on OPEN100.
attempts.evidence: 32 of 36 style measurements inside the OPEN100 range; the tracer recovers exactly the key's links on all three sheets (after two generator fixes).
attempts.why: Archived as evidence for the recorded runs; replaced by revisions B, C and D.

attempts.change: First generator version: equipment box drawn to the centre of its outline; a bubble placed inside the reactor's box.
attempts.evidence: The tracer-vs-key check failed on two sheets (the wall's outer edge joined three lines; the bubble hid its leader).
attempts.why: Both were drawing bugs, fixed in the generator, not in the tracer.

attempts.change: Revision B: draw the 19 control loops (controllers, dashed signal lines, continuation flags).
attempts.evidence: Loop audit 0 of 19 -> 19 of 19; style fidelity 32 -> 30 of 36 (instrument share 0.55-0.61 above every OPEN100 sheet).
attempts.why: Kept the loops; superseded as a drawing by revision C. The 19 of 19 is a regression check of the generator, not evidence a model can read loops.

attempts.change: Put signal lines in the scored graph file.
attempts.evidence: Failed the tracer check: 18 untraced links on sheet 101 alone.
attempts.why: Would have changed what the round-trip connection score means; signal lines live in key.json as signal_edges.

attempts.change: Control valve stations with a 60 px bypass offset.
attempts.evidence: Failed on paper before any code ran: feed-line bypasses ran through the flow controllers.
attempts.why: Offset became 45 px and the three feed lines moved apart.

attempts.change: Revision C: a station (two block valves and a bypass globe valve) around each inline control valve, as a declared drafting addition.
attempts.evidence: Style fidelity 30 -> 35 of 36; tracer recovers every key link including bypasses; loop audit still 19 of 19.
attempts.why: A drafting convention, labelled in the key; style measures resemblance to OPEN100, not engineering quality.

attempts.change: Automatic unit placement in flow order so generate.py takes any model in the schema.
attempts.evidence: First layout put every unit off the right edge (a recycle loop inflated the column count); the second stacked them in one column (utility feeds counted as starts); TE outputs byte-identical after the fix.
attempts.why: Both failures were caught by looking at the render, not by a test.

attempts.change: Source check of the seed model's names and units against teprob.f: first run.
attempts.evidence: Flagged 'Separator temperature' as wrong because the source abbreviates it to 'Sep Temp'.
attempts.why: A false alarm from the matcher.

attempts.change: First fix: an aggressive stop-word list.
attempts.evidence: It threw away the very words being compared.
attempts.why: Replaced by abbreviation handling.

attempts.change: Abbreviation handling plus a small stop-word list, tested with three planted errors.
attempts.evidence: Caught 3 of 3 planted errors; 36 of 37 items matched, 1 corrected (TI-122's name).
attempts.why: The checker was tested with known-bad input before its 'all clear' was trusted.

attempts.change: Topology check: read units, streams, directions and tag ownership from the simulator code.
attempts.evidence: 56 elements: 51 confirmed, 4 corrected (the purge S9 moved from K-101 to V-101 with its tags), 1 unresolvable (PI-116); 20 test checks including planted wrong models and edited simulator text.
attempts.why: Every row names the code line that decided it.

attempts.change: Deciding rule for split evidence: code location plus a majority of documented names.
attempts.evidence: Confirms TI-122 on the condenser and leaves PI-116 unresolved.
attempts.why: Written while looking at both cases, so it is not pre-registered.

attempts.change: Read controller identities from the comments in temain_mod.f.
attempts.evidence: 'Stripper Level Controller' sits on both the purge loop and the reactor cooling loop: comments were copied between subroutines.
attempts.why: Only the code lines are read.

attempts.change: Control loops read from the closed-loop code, checked against the recorded normal run.
attempts.evidence: 19 loops run; all 19 controlled variables within 0.34 SD of their coded setpoints, 17 within 0.07. Negative control (pairings rotated by one): 18 of 19 miss by more than 3 SD.
attempts.why: The recorded run is an independent witness to the code.

attempts.change: Renumber control valves by the loop that moves them, from one mapping at the source.
attempts.evidence: 126 replacements in 16 files; HV-205 -> FV-105, TV-211 -> FV-117; all 11 valves had carried a different loop number from their measurement.
attempts.why: Outputs rebuilt by the pipeline; each renamed valve keeps former_tag.

attempts.change: Keep indicator letters (FI, PI, ...) on transmitters that feed controllers.
attempts.evidence: Rejected the FT rename in entry 51 because the I letters were the replay points' names.
